$comment: The declared shipping method the basket and the checkout price against. ONE method, flat rates only, never a rate table: the plan's Global Constraints forbid calculated carrier rates, and live carrier rates are explicitly out of scope. BOTH AMOUNTS ARE OPERATOR-SUPPLIED COMMERCIAL FACTS, 2026-08-10 — on the same footing as every value in catalogue.json, not placeholders and not waiting on anybody. EUR 7.00 to a delivery address in an EU MEMBER STATE ('europeanUnion'), EUR 12.00 to one anywhere else ('restOfWorld'). BOTH RATES ARE NET, on the same rule as the product price (the operator, 2026-08-18): Estonian VAT is added to delivery inside the EU and to nothing else, so EUR 7.00 is EUR 8.68 on an EU buyer's bill and EUR 12.00 is EUR 12.00 everywhere else. 'ratesWithTax' carries those grossed figures as DATA, on exactly the same footing as catalogue.json's 'amountWithTax', because the gross figure is never COMPUTED here or anywhere in storefront/src: Medusa returns it on a real cart as shipping_total, and backend/src/commerce/tax-model.ts is the one place a rate is written down. backend/tests/commerce-shipping-model.test.ts derives both entries from the declared rate and the declared VAT percentage, so neither is a literal nobody owns. The two tables differ only where VAT is due, which is why 'restOfWorld' is the same figure twice rather than an omission. 'Member state' is narrower than 'in the EU', and the difference is not cosmetic: the zone is selected from the delivery address's country through storefront/mock/countries.json, whose 'euMember' flag is exactly the 27 member states, so Aland, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Reunion and Mayotte are delivery addresses in the EU that are charged the higher rate. That is also why the country field is a selection and not free text, because a rate driven from typed text charges 'eesti' the non-EU rate. The live Medusa shipping options are seeded to these two figures by backend/src/commerce/shipping-model.ts, and backend/tests/commerce-shipping-model.test.ts holds this file's two rates AND countries.json's 27 'euMember' flags to that model in both directions, so the figure this file prices with and the figure Medusa charges cannot drift apart. The dispatch and delivery estimates are NOT here: they are read verbatim from content/legal/shipping.ts, which is where they already exist.
